24 A transverse wave and a longitudinal wave both travel in the same direction down a long
stretched spring.
Which statement is not correct for these two forms of wave?
A
The displacement measurements for the particles of the two waves are made at right angles
to each other.
B
The energy transferred by the two waves is in the same direction.
C
The velocities of the two waves are in the same direction.
D
The wavelength measurements for the two waves are made at right angles to each other.

hints: Notice both waves travel in the same direction down the long stretched spring, so propagation, energy transfer and wave velocity share that direction.
Recall the defining difference: transverse means particle oscillation perpendicular to propagation, longitudinal means particle oscillation parallel to propagation.
Think about how wavelength is defined for any progressive wave - distance along the propagation direction - and compare that with how particle displacement is defined.
walkthrough: Identify the given situation: one transverse wave and one longitudinal wave both propagate in the same direction along the spring.
State the transverse rule: particles oscillate at $90^{\circ}$ to the direction of energy propagation, so displacement is across the spring.
State the longitudinal rule: particles oscillate parallel to the direction of energy propagation, so displacement is along the spring.
Combine them: particle displacements are perpendicular to each other, but energy transfer and wave propagation velocity are both down the spring in the same direction.
Recall wavelength $\lambda$ is the distance between two adjacent points oscillating in phase, measured along the propagation direction for both wave types.
Therefore the statement claiming wavelength measurements are at right angles to each other is the one that is not correct. This is option D

A.explanation: This is correct physics. Transverse particle displacement is perpendicular to travel while longitudinal particle displacement is parallel to travel, so the two displacements are at right angles.

B.explanation: This is correct physics. Both waves travel down the spring, so energy transfer by a progressive wave is along the propagation direction for both.

C.explanation: This is correct physics. Wave velocity is the velocity of propagation, which is in the same direction down the spring for both waves.

D.explanation: This is not correct. Wavelength is measured along the direction of propagation between adjacent in-phase points, so it is along the spring for both waves.
